title: BrambleX - Private Edge Readiness discussion
summary: Intro call to validate BrambleX network posture and readiness for Redwood Private (VPC). Covered peering/topology options (transit vs peering), private endpoints, egress IP requirements, region gating/data residency, KMS integration, and a pilot timeline. Agreed next step: design workshop and security pack share.
topics: KMS/HSM key flow and audit logs
action_items: Aisha Khan: Share BrambleX list of allowed egress CIDR & firewall owners by 2025-08-04
Jonah Reeves (Redwood): Draft initial network topology options (peering & transit) by 2025-08-01
Sanjay Rao: Provide SOC2 cert copy and list of required controls by 2025-08-05
next_steps: Schedule 90-minute design workshop (network + security) w/ BrambleX infra team - target week of 2025-08-04
Redwood to send security & deployment docs (SOC2, data handling, KMS guide) and a pricing anchor for Dedicated vs Private
Run a short smoke pilot in one region (us-east-1) for latency/cost baseline
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-28
Time: 09:00 PT / 12:00 ET
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Talia (Redwood Solutions), Aisha (CTO - BrambleX), Diego (Head of Platform), Lina (Network Eng), Sanjay (Security)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda: 1) understand your current infra and constraints; 2) discuss private deployment options (vpc peering, private endpoints, transit gateway); 3) next steps for pilot.
[00:18] Aisha (BrambleX): thanks maya. to give context, we run most services in aws across us-east-1 and eu-west-1. primary ask is we need an inference endpoint that never touches public internet and can be audited. low latency to our edge services in us-east is a hard req.
[00:35] Jonah (Redwood): got it. quick q: are you leaning to a fully private control plane or the private dataplane with a customer controlled VPC?
[00:45] Diego (BrambleX): we want private dataplane + customer managed VPC endpoints. control plane can be hosted if it's over private connectivity or uses SAML and ip allow-lists. need to check legal.
[01:02] Jonah: okay, good. that maps to our Redwood Private offering — we can do a customer VPC peered to our serving VPC, or we can publish interface endpoints (private link style).
[01:20] Lina (BrambleX): is there a difference in egress behaviour? our network team needs to know which side will source egress IPs for model downloads and telemetry.
[01:30] Talia (Redwood): great callout. if we do VPC peering, egress leaves from the side that initiates outbound — typically our side for managed downloads unless you host model artifacts in your s3 through cross-account role. with private endpoints we can terminate inside your vpc and egress stays in your tenancy.
[01:52] Sanjay (BrambleX): so for security we prefer egress to be predictable — a small set of static IPs we can firewall allow. can redwood provide static egress ips for a dedicated private deployment?
[02:04] Jonah: yes, for Dedicated we allocate static NAT IPs; for Private deployments on our managed network we can provide a set of egress IPs per region. if you self-host the dataplane in your vpc, your nat/egress is yours. small caveat: IPs for hosted control plane callbacks might still originate from our control plane range unless you use a private peering link.
[02:30] Aisha: timeline question — we have a compliance review in mid-aug, ideally pilot before end of august. is that realistic?
[02:40] Maya: that's tight but possible. we'll need a quick design sync, and redwood will provide security pack. key dependencies: network firewall rules, cert/key exchange, and KMS access patterns.
[02:55] Diego: about KMS — we use AWS KMS with custom key policies and want the model outputs encrypted server-side with our key. can we bring our KMS?
[03:06] Jonah: yes. we support customer-managed keys. there are two patterns: a) control plane issues requests and we wrap keys server-side with cross-account grants; b) you run the dataplane in your VPC and hold the keys locally. both have audit log implications. we'll draft the flow.
[03:25] Lina: any special port requirements? our security team restricts outbound to 443 only.
[03:31] Talia: Redwood primarily uses TLS 443 for model traffic. for peering/transit there are no additional ports required except standard mgmt ports for ops — but we can gate those behind bastion access.
[03:48] [04:00] Mateo (Customer — mislabeled Speaker): uh, sorry i'm on mobile — question, do you support cross-region peering? we want eu-west-1 kept separate for GDPR reasons.
[04:13] Aisha: yes, we need region gating — eu workloads must stay in eu-west-1 with data residency controls.
[04:20] Jonah: we do region-gating: you can pin models and serve in-region only. for a private deployment we can provision serving stacks in eu-west-1 and restrict routing policies so requests from EU remain in EU. caveat: control plane actions sometimes route to our central control plane unless you have a private control plane.
[04:42] Sanjay: do you have SOC2 and pen test docs?
[04:48] Maya: yes, we'll share SOC2 type II and our pen test summary. i'll add that to next steps.
[04:55] Diego: let's talk topology options — we use Transit Gateway in prod, and for some sandbox accounts we prefer VPC peering. what's your recommendation?
[05:08] Jonah: two common patterns: 1) Transit gateway peering to our transit — scales better for many accounts, supports routing controls and central NAT; 2) direct VPC peering is simpler for single account pairings but doesn't scale across many VPCs. for your org size (you have 5 prod VPCs plus an EU VPC) transit gateway is probably cleaner.
[05:31] Lina: any CIDR overlap concerns? we have some 10.0/8 ranges that collide with vendor networks sometimes.
[05:38] Jonah: yes, peering requires non-overlapping CIDRs. transit gateway can do route translations in some setups, but we often recommend renumbering or using NAT to avoid twisty routes. we'll surface options and implications in the design doc.
[06:00] [06:15] Aisha: curious about SLAs and fallback modes — if a region has issues, can traffic fail over to another region? we also care about model variant consistency.
[06:29] Talia: Redwood's smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants in other regions but there is a consistency tradeoff. for critical regulated flows we recommend in-region only with a canary fallback to a vetted replica. we'll capture policies per route in the rollout plan.
[06:50] Diego: latency numbers — can you give rough p50/p95 for us-east-1 when colocated in same AZ?
[06:58] Jonah: ballpark: 40–60ms p50 for 2k token chats (varies by model); p95 depends on batching and KV cache hit rates. for a colocated private dataplane you'll be low-latency, we can run a baseline during pilot.
[07:20] Sanjay: are audit logs available for every token request? our compliance needs per-request traceability for 30 days at least.
[07:30] Maya: yes we can surface token-level logging with redaction options. retention tiers are configurable — standard is 30 days, enterprise can be longer. logs can be delivered to your splunk or s3.
[07:45] Lina: network testing — will you need us to open anything for health checks or probe ports?
[07:52] Jonah: mostly 443 outbound. for health probes we use https endpoints. if we set up a private link interface endpoint, we'll require the ENI reachability checks from our side. we'll document the exact firewall rules in the workshop.
[08:10] [08:45] Aisha: question on model artifacts. we want to host models in our s3 to control lifecycle. is that supported?
[08:56] Talia: yes. you can host model artifacts in your account and we fetch via cross-account roles. that keeps artifacts in your control and may simplify compliance. we'll share the role trust policy sample.
[09:20] Diego: about data plane upgrades and maintenance windows — can you schedule maintenance to avoid our peak hours?
[09:29] Jonah: yes. for dedicated/private we offer configurable maintenance windows and can align with your blackout windows. we'll capture those in the SLA.
[09:45] Sanjay: encryption in transit and at rest — we need guarantee of TLS mutual auth for all inter-vpc connections.
[09:54] Jonah: mutual TLS is supported for control plane connections; dataplane uses mTLS for internal components when deployed in your vpc. we'll show the cert exchange flow.
[10:12] [10:30] Maya: ok i'd like to step through one end-to-end topology with you — say we deploy a private dataplane in us-east-1 using Transit Gateway. lina, what's your preferred NAT/egress pattern?
[10:45] Lina: we'd prefer central NAT in a shared services VPC and firewall egress allow rules to only a small set of IPs. ideally the vendor provides a list.
[10:55] Jonah: then the pattern is: Redwood serving VPC peers transit -> route via TGW to your shared services VPC -> central NAT egress. Redwood will publish a /32 list per region for the control plane callbacks and artifact fetches.
[11:12] Aisha: what about DNS resolution for private endpoints? we need private zone entries managed centrally.
[11:20] Talia: we support Route53 private hosted zones delegated to your account; we can coordinate zone delegation or use conditional forwarders for resolving internal endpoints.
[11:36] Diego: oof, delegation is fine but then change control — who's allowed to modify records? we need RBAC.
[11:44] Maya: we can limit DNS changes to the network ops roles and document change requests. Redwood's console supports role-based access and audit trails.
[12:00] [12:15] Lina: one more Q: what's the recommended pilot scope to validate latency, security, and scale quickly?
[12:24] Jonah: pilot: deploy a single private dataplane in us-east-1 pinned to your shared services VPC, route small traffic (10qps) from your internal service, test KV cache effectiveness and egress rules; run the security checklist. that should take 2–3 weeks if network approvals are quick.
[12:45] Aisha: sounds good. budget concern — can we get a cost anchor for Dedicated vs Private self-hosted?
[12:53] Maya: yes we'll include a cost comparison. quick note: Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and static IPs; self-hosted Private often reduces egress costs but increases your infra ops expense. we'll send an anchor.
[13:12] [13:30] Diego: any gotchas with transit gateway attachments and route limits? we have ~25 VPCs and route table complexity is something we worry about.
[13:40] Jonah: TGW route limits are real; we usually recommend grouping workloads and using route propagation planning. we'll include a route table plan and low-level options.
[13:58] Maya: i'm going to capture a few follow ups — jonah to draft 2 topology diagrams (peering + TGW) and a KMS integration flow; i'll send SOC2 + pen test; talia will add sample role policies and DNS delegation steps.
[14:20] [14:45] Sanjay: on the SOC2 and identity side, we use Okta SAML and SCIM for provisioning. can redwood integrate?
[14:55] Maya: yes we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. we'll include the SAML metadata and SCIM endpoints.
[15:12] Diego: are there any special compliance packages for financial customers — e.g., more stringent retention or encryption requirements?
[15:22] Talia: we have enterprise packages — optional higher retention, additional key attestation steps, and a private control plane option for heavy compliance. we'll include package descriptions.
[15:40] [16:00] Aisha: ok let's recap and lock in dates. we need the design workshop week of 2025-08-04 and security pack before that.
[16:12] Maya: agreed. jonah, can you confirm resource availability?
[16:16] Jonah: yes i can lead the workshop and talia will join for security/KMS. maya will do kickoff and contract followups.
[16:28] Aisha: ok final question — if we do an initial pilot, can we get some sort of SLA or credit if latency or availability doesn't meet the target?
[16:38] Maya: pilot phase is more of a tech validation; for production we offer SLA on Dedicated and Enterprise Private with credits. we'll outline pilot acceptance criteria and a path to SLA.
[16:52] [17:15] Diego: perfect, thanks all. we'll pull together the egress CIDR list and share by monday.
[17:22] Maya: thank you. we'll send the docs and schedule the workshop.
[17:30] (call ends — 58m)

Notes on transcript quality: background noise on Lina's line around 00:45; small misattribution — one speaker labeled Mateo was actually Diego. Minor stutters and filler words removed in a couple places.
crm_notes: Lead qualified for Private deployment; timeline: pilot by end of Aug; compliance gating: SOC2 docs, KMS integration, region gating for EU; next contact: schedule workshop week of 2025-08-04.
